extra.message: User-controlled pageId from URL parameter is concatenated directly into SQL query string: 'SELECT pageId, title, content FROM pages WHERE pageId='+pageId. This allows SQL injection via the /dashboard/<pageId> route.

User-controlled request.url is interpolated into a template string via .format(request.url) on line 94, then passed to render_template_string(). An attacker can inject Jinja2 template syntax (e.g. {{config}} or {{system_call('id')}}) via the URL path to achieve Server-Side Template Injection leading to remote code execution.

User input from request.form['data_obj'] is converted from hex to bytes, written to a file, and then deserialized with pickle.load(). Pickle deserialization of untrusted data allows arbitrary code execution.

User input from the URL path parameter <input> is base64-decoded and passed to yaml.load() without specifying a safe loader. yaml.load() with the default loader allows arbitrary Python object instantiation, enabling remote code execution.

os.popen(command) is registered as a Jinja2 template context processor function (system_call). This exposes OS command execution to the template engine, enabling command injection through any SSTI vector (e.g. the 404 handler SSTI via {{system_call('id')}}).

User-supplied XML from request.form['customers'] is parsed with xml.dom.pulldom.parseString() without disabling external entity resolution. This allows XML External Entity (XXE) attacks to read arbitrary files or perform SSRF.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: User-controlled fileName from request.form['example_file'] is used directly in open(fileName, 'r') and send_file(fileName) without any path validation or sanitization, allowing arbitrary file read via path traversal sequences (e.g. ../../etc/passwd).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: User-controlled file.filename is used directly in file.save('uploads/'+filename) without sanitizing path traversal sequences. An attacker can upload files to arbitrary locations using filenames like ../../../var/www/html/shell.html.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: User search input is rendered with {% autoescape false %}{{search}}{% endautoescape %}, explicitly disabling HTML auto-escaping. Combined with the controller passing request.form.get('search') directly, this allows reflected XSS.
The X-XSS-Protection header is explicitly set to '0', disabling the browser's built-in XSS filter. This removes a defense-in-depth mechanism against reflected XSS attacks.

Content from deserialized pickle data is rendered with {% autoescape false %}{{content}}{% endautoescape %}, disabling HTML auto-escaping. An attacker who controls the deserialized data can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript.

User-supplied link (item[3]) from the messaging form is placed directly in an href attribute: <a target="_blank" href="{{item[3]}}">. Jinja2 auto-escaping does not filter javascript: URIs, enabling stored XSS via links like javascript:alert(1).
Authentication uses hardcoded credentials: password == "admin" and username == "admin". An attacker who discovers these credentials can fully bypass authentication.
Flask SECRET_KEY is set to the trivial value 'random', which allows an attacker to forge session cookies. With knowledge of this key, arbitrary session data (including 'loggedin') can be injected.

The /webmaster endpoint sets session['loggedin'] = random without any authentication check. Any unauthenticated user can visit /webmaster to obtain a valid session and then access /confidential, completely bypassing the login.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The authentication check if(session['loggedin']) will raise a KeyError if the user has no session, and does not validate the session value's authenticity. Combined with the /webmaster route setting this session variable without auth, the confidential page is fully accessible to unauthenticated users.

Login error messages differentiate between invalid username (line 18-19) and invalid password (line 20-21), allowing user enumeration. An attacker can determine valid usernames by observing which error message is returned.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Flask debug mode is enabled (app.debug = True), which exposes the Werkzeug interactive debugger in production. This debugger allows arbitrary Python code execution through its console.

CORS is configured with resources={r"/*": {"origins": "*"}}, allowing any origin to access all endpoints. Combined with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials on the /confidential endpoint, this could enable cross-origin data theft.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The /confidential endpoint sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Combined with the wildcard CORS policy, this could allow cross-origin requests with credentials to access sensitive confidential data.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The webmaster template contains hardcoded credentials (Mark/Thisismysecretpass, Jacob/BirdLover1, Larry/Letmein123) displayed in plaintext HTML. Since the /webmaster route has no authentication, these credentials are exposed to all visitors.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
